entries.title: Psalms 71:1
segments: In its general character, this psalm agrees with

, and is to be interpreted upon the same principles. 
 

 
Trust in the Lord is the sure means of safety to his people, and their habitual resort in time of trouble.

entries.title: Psalms 71:6
segments: God is our maker, our preserver, and the giver of all our mercies.  On him we ever have been and must be dependent for all good, and to him we should be habitually devoted.

entries.title: Psalms 71:7
segments: I am as a wonder unto many; an object of astonishment from the intensity of my sufferings.  These words were strikingly fulfilled in the person of our Lord, the great Head of the church.
They are fulfilled also in each of his members, according to the measure of "the afflictions of Christ," which God has appointed him to "fill up."

entries.title: Psalms 71:9
segments: Old age is a time when men peculiarly need the presence and favor of God, and he will not cast off any who truly trust in him.

entries.title: Psalms 71:11
segments: God hath forsaken him; this they concluded from his distresses.

entries.title: Psalms 71:13
segments: Let them be confounded; see note to

entries.title: Psalms 71:15
segments:
The numbers; the number of his mercies. 
 
The mercies of God are innumerable, and call for habitual thanksgiving.

entries.title: Psalms 71:20
segments:
Shalt quicken me again; grant him deliverance from trouble and give him prosperity. 
 
  From the depths of the earth; from the deep waters of the earth, put here as a symbol of great distress.
However great the present trials of God's people, they may rejoice in the anticipation of being one day delivered, and made conquerors and more than conquerors over all their foes.

entries.title: Psalms 71:22
segments: Psaltery; a stringed instrument of music.
